title: Scaena theme (design system)
description: Tokens, typographic roles, layout templates, motion, and palettes. Documents reference these by name; they never store resolved values. See docs/SPEC.md §3.6.

formats.description: The grid in other formats than the deck's own (SPEC §3.4): `"9:16": { "grid": … }`. Each layout says its own slots there.

code.description: How code is set and colored (theme format 0.18, ADR-0029): the role a code text is set in, its tab stops, and each kind of token's look.

furniture.description: A slide's number and footer: where each stands and in what type, and the layouts a slide shows neither on (theme format 0.14, ADR-0028). The deck says whether they show.

pictures.description: How its pictures are framed (theme format 0.21, PLAN T.3a, ADR-0031): every image takes the frame, and no image says otherwise. None where it says none.

drift.description: In shorter sides of the rect.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise from up: a linear gradient's direction (180, the default, runs top to bottom), a conic one's start.

x.description: A radial or conic gradient's center across the rect, 0 to 1 within it, and as far as its width again either side outside it (deck format 0.34).

y.description: A radial or conic gradient's center down the rect, likewise.

radius.description: A radial gradient's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

speed.description: Degrees a second a linear or conic gradient turns.

octaves.description: Layers of finer noise over the first (fractal Brownian motion); 1 is plain simplex noise.

speed.description: How fast the field changes, in noise cycles a second.

contrast.description: How far the field spreads across the palette.

fps.description: How many times a second the grain changes; 0 holds it still.

size.description: A particle's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

softness.description: How much of a particle's radius its edge fades over.

scale.description: A cell of the light's network, in shorter sides of the rect.

speed.description: How fast the light wobbles and flows.

intensity.description: How far along the palette a line's middle reaches.

roles.description: Color roles, each the name of a color token.

shadow.description: The shadows a node may cast (PLAN 2.115), by name: `soft`, `raised`, and `floating` in the shipped themes, as a presentation app offers an object's shadow.

Shadow.description: A shadow a node casts (PLAN 2.115): how far it falls from the node, right and down, how soft its edge is, its color, and how dark it is.

x.description: How far right of the node it falls, canvas units; left where it is negative.

y.description: How far below the node it falls, canvas units; above where it is negative.

blur.description: How soft its edge is, canvas units: the blur's radius, twice the deviation of the Gaussian it is drawn with.

color.description: Its color: black where it names none.

opacity.description: How dark it is, from 0 to 1.

lists.description: How a text's list items are marked and indented (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0018).

Family.description: A font family: its file in the bundle and how it may vary.

italic.description: Its italic face (SPEC §3.5), which text set `italic` takes. A family without one sets such text upright: no italic is synthesized (lint W231).

upright.description: Upright by design: the family has no italic because its script sets none, as Japanese and Korean do not (ADR-0031, call 6), so it names none. A family that names no italic without saying so has merely lost it. Text set `italic` in either is set upright, and lint W231 says so all the same.

whole.description: Kept whole: a save never subsets the family's files, its italic's among them (ADR-0031, call 5). A font whose license reserves its name, as Pretendard's does, may not carry the name in a subset, which the OFL counts a Modified Version (OFL 1.1, condition 3).

fallback.description: Other families in this theme, in order. Bundle-only; system fonts are never consulted.

Face.description: Another face of a family, in a file of its own: its italic (PLAN 2.40). Its file names the family's name, as the family's own file does.

Role.description: What a text role looks like (SPEC §3.5).

italic.description: Set in its family's italic face (SPEC §3.5); upright when unset.

leading.description: Line height as a multiple of size.

snap.description: What of the text sits on the baseline grid (`grid.baseline`, SPEC §3.4): every baseline, or the first line's cap height. Nothing snaps when unset.

color.description: Color role or token; defaults to onSurface.

Wrap.description: How a text's lines break where its words run past its width (SPEC §3.5).

Snap.description: What of a text role sits on the baseline grid (SPEC §3.4).

oneOf.description: Every line's baseline, the lines whole grid lines apart: body text.
The first line's cap height, the lines below at the role's leading: display text.

Lists.description: A theme's lists (ADR-0018): how far each level's words start from the one above, and the least room between a marker and its words, both in ems of the text's size; a bullet for each level, and a pattern for each level's numbers, whose first `1`, `a`, `A`, `i`, or `I` is the item's number in digits, letters, or roman numerals. A level past a list's end takes its last.

baseline.description: Baseline grid: the distance between its lines in cu, which run from the top margin. Text roles with `snap` sit on it.

Margin.description: One margin for every side, or 2–4 CSS-style.

Layout.description: A layout template: named slots on the grid.

name.description: What a person calls it in an editor (theme format 0.12, PLAN 3.31): `SWOT`, `Two by two`, `Q&A`. An editor without one makes a name of its key.

group.description: Where an editor's gallery of slides to start offers it (theme format 0.11, PLAN 3.30): a section named for what the layouts in it hold (`Titles`, `Words`, `Pictures`), in the order the theme first names each.

formats.description: The slots that move in other formats (SPEC §3.4): `"9:16": { "slots": … }`.

LayoutFormat.description: A layout in another format: slots that take the place of its slots of the same names there. The rest stay as they are.

role.description: Default text role for nodes placed in this slot.

inset.description: How far in from its cells the slot stands, canvas units (theme format 0.11, PLAN 3.30): one number on each side, words on a card that fills the same cells; or each side its own (theme format 0.27), as words under a text set on the foot of its cells stand clear of its descenders.

prompt.description: What goes in the slot (theme format 0.11, PLAN 3.30). Words a person types over: a new slide in the layout puts a text in the slot's `role` there, with these words, each item of a list a paragraph. A slot with no role says in words what goes in it, a picture or a figure, and a new slide leaves it empty, an editor outlining it. A shape: a new slide puts one there, under what is placed in the slots over it, a card or a rule. A format's slot keeps the layout's prompt.

bleed.description: The slot reaches the canvas's edge on each side where its tracks meet the edge of the grid (theme format 0.11, PLAN 3.30): a picture that bleeds, off the page or one side of it.

example.description: What the layout's picture shows in a slot that waits for a picture or a figure (theme format 0.12, PLAN 3.31): a picture, drawn by one of the theme's shader presets; or a chart of a kind, or a table, drawn from a few rows of their own. An editor draws each layout with these in its slots, so its picture shows what the slot is for. A new slide in the layout leaves the slot waiting all the same.

fit.description: How a text placed in the slot fits it where the text does not say (theme format 0.13): `shrink` sets a number too wide for its slot smaller, down to its role's `minSize`, as a presentation app's placeholder shrinks what is typed in it to fit.

Range.description: A grid index or an inclusive [start, end] range (1-based).

Align.description: Alignment within a slot or cell. Vertical anchors include typographic ones (SPEC §3.4).

SlotInset.description: How far in from its cells a slot stands: the same on each side, or each side its own (theme format 0.27), a side left out none.

Sides.description: Each side's own inset, canvas units.

Prompt.description: What goes in a slot (PLAN 3.30): words, a paragraph to each line; a list's items; or a shape.

PromptItems.description: A list's items, as a slot's prompt gives them: `{ "bullet": [...] }` or `{ "number": [...] }`.

PromptShape.description: A shape a new slide puts in a slot (PLAN 3.30): a card behind words, a rule between them, an arrow from one to the next, or an icon over an item's words (PLAN G.23).

fill.description: What fills a rectangle, an ellipse, a polygon, or an icon: a color token or role. A line and an arrow take the theme's rule.

stroke.description: What strokes its outline, a color token or role, in the theme's thin rule (theme format 0.12, PLAN 3.31): a ring, or circles that overlap and leave what is under them seen.

points.description: Its points, as fractions of the slot: `[0, 0]` its top left, `[1, 1]` its bottom right (theme format 0.12, PLAN 3.31). A line or an arrow with none crosses the slot's middle, left to right; one down the slot, or back, gives them. A polygon gives three or more.

icon.description: An icon's name, as the set it is drawn from names it (theme format 0.15, PLAN G.23): what the icon a new slide puts there is called, by a reader and in the layers.

path.description: An icon's outline, as SVG path data (theme format 0.15, PLAN G.23), drawn on its `view`.

view.description: The box of an icon's `path` that fits the slot, `[x, y, w, h]`, as a path shape's `view` fits its node (theme format 0.15, PLAN G.23): the icon as large as the slot takes, in its middle.

PromptShapeKind.description: The shapes a slot's prompt makes.

oneOf.description: Theme format 0.12: a chevron, a triangle, or any outline its `points` give.

Theme format 0.15 (PLAN G.23): an icon, its `path` drawn on its `view` and named by `icon`. A new slide puts it there for a person to swap for another; a deck made from a prompt puts there the icon its item names.

Rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in canvas units.

Example.description: What a layout's picture shows in a slot that waits (PLAN 3.31): `{ "picture": "backdrop" }`, `{ "chart": "bar" }`, `{ "table": 3 }`, or `{ "map": "backdrop" }` (theme format 0.22).

oneOf.description: A picture, drawn by the theme's shader preset of this name.
A chart of this kind, of a few rows made up for it.
A table of this many columns, of a few rows made up for it: seven are a week's days, a month's calendar (theme format 0.18, PLAN S.2).
A map's place (ADR-0030, PLAN O.1e, theme format 0.22): the picture this shader preset draws, with a pin and a label over it, and no provider's map. Insert › Map… fills the place.

ChartKind.description: v1 chart kinds (SPEC §3.7); waffle and heatmap are deferred. A `slope` compares two states, a line a series from the first to the second, both ends labeled and the change said; a `range` spans the value axis at each category, a dumbbell between its series or each value with its `interval` (PLAN 1.30); a `weather` chart draws a forecast, a column for each period, its sky's icon and its figures (ADR-0030).

TextFit.description: What a text node does when its text does not fit (SPEC §3.4).

ThemeFormat.description: A theme in another format: the grid there.

maxBuild.description: Max total choreography per state, ms (lint W321).

Preset.description: A named entrance, exit, or emphasis: keyframes with parameters.

from.description: The look an entrance starts from, or an exit ends at.

to.description: The look an emphasis goes out to.

PresetLook.description: A motion preset's look (SPEC §3.9), against the unit at rest: what an entrance starts from, an exit ends at, and an emphasis goes out to and comes back from.

color.description: A theme color every paint the unit draws mixes toward, in Oklab, keeping its alpha.

LookTransform.description: A look's transform: scale, then rotate, about `anchor`, then translate.

anchor.description: Fractions of the unit's box; its center by default.

Color.description: Theme token name (e.g. "accent", "color.ink") or a literal (#rrggbb[aa], oklch(...)). Literals outside overrides are lint W300.

LookParams.description: Numbers a look sets on what its unit draws.

progress.description: How much of each outline a shape strokes is drawn, from where the outline starts.

Duration.description: Milliseconds, or a named theme duration ("fast", "standard", "slow").

Easing.description: Named theme easing or a cubic Bézier [x1, y1, x2, y2].

SplitUnit.description: What a choreographed entrance splits its target into. A text's `paragraphs` are the stretches its hard line breaks end, a list's items (deck format 0.27, theme format 0.17).

ShaderPreset.description: A shader a node can name (SPEC §3.8): its kind, and the palette and params a node of that kind takes unless it sets its own.

palette.description: A shader palette from this theme.

ShaderParam.description: A shader parameter: a number, or a name its kind lists (a gradient's `shape`).

Charts.description: Chart styling: every chart draws with these, never with literals.

label.description: Value labels: their role (`label` when unset), and which values print when a chart does not say (`auto` when unset: by kind).

title.description: Axis titles; their role defaults to the axis's.

tickCount.description: About how many ticks a value axis shows (d3's tick count); 5 when unset.

maxTicks.description: At most how many ticks, and so reference lines, a value axis shows; 5 when unset. The axis asks for `tickCount`, then for fewer, down to two, until its ticks fit.

signal.description: The signal color: the one hue a chart spends on what matters, the data a highlight picks out; `accent` when unset. The rest of the data is the categorical palette, which a theme keeps neutral.

groupGap.description: Between the bars of one category's group, a fraction of each bar's slot; 0.1 when unset.

pointRadius.description: A dot on each point of a line; none when unset.

dotRadius.description: A dot plot's dots, and a scatter's at its largest size; 8 when unset.

donutHole.description: A donut's hole, a fraction of its radius; 0.6 when unset.

legend.description: Legends: their role (the axis's when unset), and where a chart that does not say places one (`direct` when unset).

annotation.description: Annotations: rules, bands, callouts, and highlights.

projected.description: Forecasts and estimates (PLAN 1.28): how a line dashes through what is projected, how much lighter an area is under it, and what its value labels add.

ChartRule.description: A chart rule: the axis or the gridlines.

ChartValues.description: How value labels read, and which print when a chart does not say (SPEC §3.7).

LabelShow.description: Which values a chart prints. `auto` (the theme's `charts.label.show`, else by kind) puts the data on the marks: every bar, dot, and slice; a line's or an area's first and last; a scatter's none.

ChartLegend.description: How legends read, and where they stand when a chart does not say (SPEC §3.7).

LegendPlace.description: Where a legend stands. `auto` is the theme's `charts.legend.place`, else `direct`. `direct` names each series at its end, beside the plot, where a chart has ends: a line, an area, or a stacked bar; any other chart places it `top`.

ChartAnnotation.description: How a chart's annotations look (SPEC §3.7), every one a role, a token, or a fraction.

role.description: The text's role; the value labels' when unset.

stroke.description: A rule's and a callout's leader's stroke; `thin` when unset.

color.description: The rules, the leaders, the bands, and the text; `accent` when unset.

opacity.description: A rule's and a leader's opacity; 1 when unset.

band.description: A band's fill opacity; 0.12 when unset.

dimmed.description: The opacity a highlight leaves the rest of the chart's marks at; 0.5 when unset. Their value labels and names dim half as far, so they stay legible.

ChartProjected.description: How a chart shows the rows its `projected` marks (SPEC §3.7).

dash.description: A line's dash and the gap after it, in widths of the line; [3, 2] when unset.

opacity.description: An area's fill under projected rows, a fraction of its own; 0.5 when unset.

note.description: What a projected value's label says after the value; `est.` when unset.

Tables.description: Table styles (SPEC §3.6), every one a role, a token, or a length.

header.description: The header row's text: role `label` in `onSurfaceMuted` when unset.

cell.description: The cells' text: role `body` in its own color when unset. Numbers set in tabular lining figures.

rule.description: The rule under the header: the `hairline` stroke in `onSurfaceMuted` when unset.

rowRule.description: Rules between rows; none when unset.

rowGap.description: Canvas units above and below each row's text; half a space unit when unset.

columnGap.description: Canvas units between columns; an em of the cell text when unset.

stretch.description: Whether a table spans its cell, its first column taking the room the cell has to spare; false when unset: a table is as wide as its columns, at the cell's start.

TableText.description: A table's text: a role, and a color token or role.

CodeLook.description: How code is set and colored (SPEC §3.6, ADR-0029; theme format 0.18). A kind of token the theme names no color for takes one derived from its accent, and every color code is drawn in is held, where it is drawn, to read on its ground.

role.description: The text role a code text is set in where it names none: the theme's `code` role when unset, else `body`.

tab.description: The columns between tab stops; 4 when unset.

syntax.description: Each kind of token's look, by the kind's name.

card.description: The card a code text stands on (PLAN 2.136, theme format 0.26): where unset, `surface-2` stepped from the surface to 1.3:1, square, 32 cu in.

numbers.description: How a code text's line numbers are set: their color and the room between them and the code (PLAN 2.136, theme format 0.26).

focus.description: How the lines out of a code text's focus are set back, and what marks those in it (PLAN 2.140, theme format 0.28).

Syntax.description: Each kind of token's look in code (ADR-0029), by the kind's name: the 16 kinds the scanners read. A kind left out is derived.

SyntaxLook.description: A kind of token's look in code: its color, weight, and italic, each the derived one where unset.

color.description: A color token or role, or a literal, which a theme may hold: drawn a step lighter or darker where its ground needs it to read.

weight.description: Its weight: else the text's, and 600 at least for a keyword.

italic.description: Whether it is set in its family's italic face, where the family has one: else as the text is, and in italic for a comment.

CodeCard.description: The card a code text stands on (ADR-0029): a rect that hugs the code and its gutter, `inset` in from its edges.

fill.description: Its color, a color token or role: `surface-2` stepped from the surface to 1.3:1 where unset, so it shows on a projector.

radius.description: Its corners' radius, a step of the theme's radius scale or canvas units: square where unset.

inset.description: The room between its edges and the code, canvas units: 32 where unset.

stroke.description: Its outline's color, a color token or role: none where unset.

shadow.description: The shadow it casts, one of the theme's `tokens.shadow`: none where unset.

Length.description: A length in canvas units, a token reference (e.g. "space.4"), or a percentage string.

CodeNumbers.description: How a code text's line numbers are set (ADR-0029).

color.description: Their color, a color token or role: the muted text color where unset. Held to read on the card, as the code's colors are.

gap.description: The room between the numbers and the code, in ems of the code's size: 1 where unset.

CodeFocus.description: How a walkthrough sets back the lines out of focus (ADR-0029): each token's color mixed toward its ground, never under 3:1, and the band behind the lines in focus.

dim.description: How far each token out of focus is mixed toward its ground, 0 to 1: 0.55 where unset.

band.description: The color of a band behind the lines in focus, a color token or role: none where unset. The code in focus is held to read on it.

Furniture.description: A slide's furniture (theme format 0.14, ADR-0028): its number and its footer, each set in a text role in the margin at the canvas's foot or head, across columns of the grid.

number.description: Where the slide's number stands, where the deck shows it.

footer.description: Where the deck's footer stands, where the deck has one.

except.description: The layouts a slide in shows neither, unless it says so (a title, a divider, a picture that bleeds to the foot).

FurnitureItem.description: One piece of a slide's furniture: a line of words in the margin.

col.description: The grid's columns it spans, in each format's grid.

edge.description: The margin it stands in: the canvas's foot, or its head.

role.description: The text role it is set in.

align.description: How it lines up across its columns; start by default.

color.description: A color token or role it is set in, in place of its role's color.

pattern.description: How the number is written: `{n}` the slide's number, `{total}` how many slides the deck has (`"{n} / {total}"`); `{n}` by default. The footer's words are the deck's.

Edge.description: The margin a piece of furniture stands in.

Across.description: How a piece of furniture lines up across its columns.

Pictures.description: How a theme frames its pictures (PLAN T.3a).

Frame.description: A picture's frame: `none`, or a mat of a theme color around it, a keyline at its edge, or both, drawn inside the image's box, the picture inset by them.

Framing.description: A frame's bands, from the picture out: its keyline, then its mat.

mat.description: A band of color around the picture, as a print's mat.

keyline.description: A thin line at the picture's edge, between it and the mat.

Band.description: A band of a frame: a color token or role, and how wide it is, canvas units.
